title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention (timeouts)
author: Ava Thompson
description: Context: We observed several tail-latency incidents where long-running heavy prompts could starve small latency-sensitive requests when the continuous-batcher used FIFO queueing. Motivation: Improve queueing fairness and prevent starvation without regressing throughput or increasing p99 for typical workloads. This PR introduces scheduler tuning for the continuous batcher: 1) request aging and dynamic priority bumping to prevent starvation of small/old requests, 2) configurable per-tenant and per-route fairness windows, 3) adaptive timeouts to break up oversized requests into multiple passes, and 4) observability hooks and metrics for queue depth, wait-time percentiles, and fairness anomalies. Design summary: - Add RequestAgeTracker: increments age per scheduling cycle and exposes age histogram. - Implement priority ramp: requests older than age_threshold get exponential priority multiplier up to max_priority. - Introduce queue buckets by size-class (small/medium/large) and apply a weighted round-robin scheduler across buckets to avoid head-of-line blocking. - Add route-level configurable parameters: max_wait_ms, age_threshold_ms, priority_multiplier, and enable_adaptive_timeouts. - Adaptive timeout flow: if request exceeds max_wait_ms and is still large, split the request at the token boundary and enqueue continuation with preserved KV cache state. - Backwards-compatible config: defaults preserve prior behavior; feature flag continuous_batcher.fairness_enabled=false keeps legacy FIFO. Testing and benchmarks: microbenchmarks on dev-lab with gpt-like open weights show <=1% throughput regression and p99 improvement for small requests by 18-28% under mixed workloads. Canary rollout: staged rollout to dedicated pool -> 10% hosted traffic -> 50% -> global. Production rollback path included. Notes: this is a behaviorally significant change to scheduling but not a breaking API change. See linked linear tasks for follow-ups (metrics dashboards + rollout tuning).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Can you explain how the priority multiplier is bounded to avoid priority inversion? RequestAuthor: We cap multiplier at max_priority (default 8x) and combine with weighted RR such that a single aged request cannot fully starve others; added unit tests that simulate inversion.

Priya Nair: How do we ensure KV cache correctness across timeout-split continuations? RequestAuthor: The splitter preserves KV cache handles and shaded metadata; we added tests and a KV cache lifecycle hook to reattach continuations safely.

Omar Khalid: CI showed a flaky test on integration; was that addressed? RequestAuthor: Yes—flakiness was due to clock-based timing; swapped to simulation clock and increased test tolerance; re-ran suite and CI passed.
SRE (comment): Suggest adding an alert for fairness_violation_count > 10/min during rollout. RequestAuthor: Added alert note to docs and created ENG-1180 to track alert tuning.

release_notes: Improves continuous-batcher scheduling fairness: prevents starvation of small/latency-sensitive requests, adds adaptive timeouts and request splitting, exposes new metrics for queue wait times and age. Defaults preserve legacy behavior unless fairness_enabled is turned on.
